name: Client Settings
desc: Client sends its locale, view distance, chat mode, chat colors, difficulty preference, and cape visibility.
notes: Sent by vanilla client every time settings change. The server stores locale for player language detection. View distance affects how many chunks the server sends. Rise 6.0 ClientSpoofer sends spoofed C15 to change the locale string for server-side language detection bypass and to set a fake view distance.

writeup.p: C15 declares client preferences: locale string, render distance byte, chat visibility enum, chat colors flag and a model-part bitmask. Vanilla re-sends it from GameSettings whenever any of those settings change, and the server stores the values on the player. It is the only serverbound packet that carries the client's locale, which makes it the hook for server-side language detection.

processClientSettings delegates to EntityPlayerMP.handleClientSettings, which stores translator (locale), chatVisibility and chatColours on the player and pushes the model-part flags into DataWatcher slot 10. The render distance byte is parsed but not stored by the bundled 1.8.9 handler; chunk streaming distance stays server-configured. The locale is what language-detection plugins read.

None of the 8 clients ships a locale-spoof module; the corpus hits are indirect. Rise 6.x PingSpoofComponent lists C15 in its blink tuple so settings packets are held and replayed during blink spoofs, and the script PacketAPI exposes sendSettings(). Spicy's Bhop imports C15 without using it. Clients known to cancel C15 for locale bypasses exist outside this corpus.

The packet is informational and server-validated trivially, so abuse is limited to two corners: re-sending it to reset the server's stored locale after a language change (defeating per-locale chat filters), and the blink interaction, where holding C15 for the blink window freezes the server's view of client settings. The model-part bitmask is the only field that reaches other players (via DataWatcher), so a corrupted mask is the only client-visible side effect.

implementation.overview: The settings declaration packet. No locale-spoof module exists in the 8 clients; C15 shows up only inside Rise 6.x's blink-hold component and the script PacketAPI, plus dead imports in Spicy Bhop.
implementation.server_handling: processClientSettings -> EntityPlayerMP.handleClientSettings: stores locale, chat visibility and colors; model-part flags go to DataWatcher slot 10 (broadcast to other players). Render distance is parsed and discarded in the bundled 1.8.9 sources. No validation beyond String length.
implementation.protocol_notes: String locale + byte viewDistance + byte chatVisibility enum + bool colors + byte modelPartFlags (bitmask for cape/jacket/sleeves/pants/hat). Re-sent on every settings change, so a settings GUI session naturally emits several. The locale is a plain String and is never matched against a known list.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: No anti-cheat measures C15. Language-detection and anti-spam plugins key off the locale string; spoofing it changes plugin behavior, not server physics. The blink-hold interaction matters to anti-cheats only insofar as the same component also holds C03 and C0F packets, which is where the actual detection signal lives.

modules.name: PingSpoofComponent (blink hold)
modules.purpose: Hold C15 (with C13, C17, C18, C19 and movement packets) while the client blinks, then replay it in order.
modules.how_it_works: C15 is in the blink class tuple. When blink() enables the regular and blink tuples, onPacket cancels matching packets and parks them with a timestamp; PostMotionEvent replays entries whose delay elapsed and dispatch() flushes the rest on world change.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Holding C15 is invisible; the component's value is holding C0F/C00/C03 together so the server sees a consistent, delayed stream. The blink window is what movement anti-cheats measure.

modules.name: PacketAPI (script bridge)
modules.purpose: Expose a settings re-declaration to the scripting layer.
modules.how_it_works: sendSettings() constructs a default C15PacketClientSettings and sends it via PacketUtil.send.
modules.vanilla_hook: No event hook; direct PacketUtil.send from script code.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: None; a default settings packet is indistinguishable from a vanilla re-send.

implementation.general_hooks: No module-level C15 hook in the corpus; the packet is handled by component infrastructure (Rise 6.x) or script calls.
implementation.client_variations: Vanilla GameSettings emits C15 on settings change in every client; Rise 6.x adds the blink tuple and script bridge. Spicy Bhop carries dead imports of C15 (and C14, C17, C18, C19) with no call sites.
